comments.author: Jaxander
comments.body_html:
So after testing this, I actually don’t think that is correct. In SPT\SPT_Data\Configs\location.json, I can see the following values:

“looseLootMultiplier”: { “bigmap”: 2.5, “develop”: 1, “factory4_day”: 3.5, “factory4_night”: 3.5, “interchange”: 2.8, “laboratory”: 2.8, “rezervbase”: 2.9, “shoreline”: 3.7, “woods”: 1.9, “hideout”: 0, “lighthouse”: 2.8, “privatearea”: 1, “suburbs”: 1, “tarkovstreets”: 3, “terminal”: 1, “sandbox”: 2.8, “sandbox_high”: 2.8, “town”: 0, “labyrinth”: 3 },

I thought this mod’s config values were multiplicative on top of these, but after testing, I think they just override these values. Testing Interchange after multiple runs and reading the server log for items generated, I found this:

Without this mod, around 350-500 loose items generated in each raid. With this mod installed and Interchange’s “LooseLootMultiplier” value set to 1, around 120-200 loose items spawned. Playing through the map you could feel how sparse it suddenly was. Way less than unaltered spawns. With this mod installed and the value set to 2.8 (the same value listed in, loose items again started to show up in normal values of 350-500. So I think “100% spawns” for Interchange is matching it to its value in locations.json, not setting it to 1.

The mod’s default value of 5 on each map would be an increase, but not a 500% increased. On some maps it would be less than double. If you set every value to 1, you might think you’d be getting 100% the vanilla amount, as I thought, but really you’d be getting far less, sometimes as little as about 25%. If you wanted 5x the loot, you’d need to change them all differently. Factory for instance would need to be 17.5. And of course you would need to turn on overlapping loot to get a more accurate value, otherwise it trends lower than that.

tl;dr I’m pretty sure after testing that the above per-map values, not 1, are “100%” vanilla loot. “1” won’t get you 100%, “5” won’t get you 500%.
